pill.desc: colorless to pale yellow solution in a prefilled syringe

clues.kinetics: Serum concentrations are approximately 90,000-fold lower than vitreous concentrations. No dose adjustment is needed for renal impairment.
clues.substance: Recombinant and humanized, made in an Escherichia coli expression system at about 48 kilodaltons. Supplied as a preservative-free sterile solution.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA as single-dose prefilled syringes in two strengths, given once a month.
clues.safety: No boxed warning; contraindicated with ocular or periocular infections or hypersensitivity. Conjunctival hemorrhage and eye pain are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: Wet age-related macular degeneration, macular edema after retinal vein occlusion, diabetic macular edema and retinopathy, and myopic choroidal neovascularization.
clues.mechanism: Binds VEGF-A and blocks its interaction with VEGFR1 and VEGFR2 on endothelial cells, reducing vascular leakage and new vessel formation.

tell: Made in Escherichia coli and injected into the eye, this VEGF-A binder has a vitreous half-life of about 9 days.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: maximum serum concentrations are predicted to be reached at approximately 1 day
evidence.pk.halfLifeH: the estimated average vitreous elimination half-life was approximately 9 days
evidence.pk.cmax: mean (±SD) maximum ranibizumab serum concentrations were 1.7 (± 1.1) ng/mL

evidence.biologic: a recombinant humanized IgG1 kappa isotype monoclonal antibody fragment
